recommendations.label: Heavy design
recommendations.definition: Architecture, non-trivial refactoring, and hard problem-solving across interacting concepts.
recommendations.outcomeMeasure: Executable contract checks plus substantive review grade and semantic-reissue rate.
recommendations.benchmarkStatus: Planned class-specific suite; canonical policy baseline is active.
neverDowngradeWhen: P0, security, distributed authority, destructive migration, or credible data loss requires Sol/xhigh.
Architecture uncertainty is not a cost-based downgrade signal.
recommendations.rationale: Sol/medium is the demanding-work policy tier with the strongest favorable historical signal; concrete hard-floor triggers raise the card to Sol/xhigh.

evidence.summary: Five known Sol/medium chore/feature grades were all A/B and seven runs had no reissues; this is not a controlled heavy-design cohort.

recommendations.label: Feature and bug implementation
recommendations.definition: Everyday feature implementation and ordinary bug repair with an executable verification seam.
recommendations.outcomeMeasure: Native fixture pass rate across isolated controlled repair scenarios.
recommendations.benchmarkStatus: Controlled pilot complete; below the 20-sample validation gate.
downgradeWhen: The change is reversible and contained to one subsystem.
The requirement and deterministic verification path are explicit.
The concrete card score is at most 50 and no hard floor applies.
neverDowngradeWhen: An unclear bug requires at least Terra/medium.
A public protocol, persistent-state migration, or three runtime subsystems requires at least Sol/medium.
recommendations.rationale: Across four checked-in hard-coding scenarios, Sol/medium resolved 9 of 12 attempts versus 2 of 12 for Terra/medium and 4 of 12 for the provider fallback. This small controlled cohort supports a pilot recommendation, not universal superiority.

costPerSuccessfulOutcome.note: Catalog list-price estimate from retained subject-model usage; local deterministic test CPU is excluded.

evidence.summary: Three attempts per route on an end-boundary defect.
Three attempts per route on culture-independent Unicode normalization.
Three attempts per route on a cross-file wire contract.
Three attempts per route on an underspecified repair; no route passed.

recommendations.label: Mechanical chore
recommendations.definition: Rote, locally specified edits such as renames, formatting, narrow fixture updates, and boilerplate.
recommendations.outcomeMeasure: Exact diff contract plus deterministic regression command.
recommendations.benchmarkStatus: Planned class-specific suite; Luna has no qualifying cohort.
neverDowngradeWhen: An unclear bug, public contract, security boundary, migration, concurrency, or distributed state is not a mechanical chore.
recommendations.rationale: Luna/medium is the canonical cost-saving route for trivial, local, mechanically verified work, but remains explicitly provisional until controlled evidence exists.

evidence.summary: No Luna cohort existed in the historical benchmark; the route is an explicitly unvalidated hypothesis.

recommendations.label: Documentation edit
recommendations.definition: Prose, comments, changelogs, and release notes with local factual sources.
recommendations.outcomeMeasure: Fact checklist, link check, terminology consistency, and substantive review grade.
recommendations.benchmarkStatus: Planned class-specific suite; canonical policy baseline is active.
neverDowngradeWhen: Broad synthesis, policy interpretation, or missing source facts must be rescored rather than treated as a local doc edit.
recommendations.rationale: A local, source-backed prose edit has the same cheap-verification shape as the Luna/medium mechanical tier; no controlled documentation cohort yet qualifies that prior.

evidence.summary: The cheapest-tier hypothesis is bounded by exact source facts and deterministic checks; it is not a measured doc-class winner.

recommendations.label: Research and investigation
recommendations.definition: Reading code, documentation, and history to answer a question or produce an evidence-backed analysis.
recommendations.outcomeMeasure: Fact-recall and inference rubric against a hidden answer key, with citation precision.
recommendations.benchmarkStatus: Planned class-specific suite; canonical policy baseline is active.
downgradeWhen: The corpus is compact, the question is closed, and the answer key is deterministic.
The concrete card score is at most 50 and no hard floor applies.
neverDowngradeWhen: Broad context reconstruction, architecture history, or unknown root cause keeps the work at Sol/medium or above.
recommendations.rationale: Broad investigation is a declared Sol/medium use case; Terra/medium is available only for bounded, closed-corpus research with cheap verification.

evidence.summary: Sol/medium has the strongest favorable historical signal for demanding analysis, without a controlled research cohort.

recommendations.label: Quality Studio review
recommendations.definition: Legacy Quality Studio review traffic whose operational sighting outcomes use a separate evidence contract.
recommendations.outcomeMeasure: Confirmed-finding precision from QS dossiers; controlled seeded-defect recall is reported under source-code review.
recommendations.benchmarkStatus: No eligible operational QS cohort; policy baseline only.
neverDowngradeWhen: Do not infer recall from confirmed-versus-dismissed findings.
Do not route from the excluded QS fixture.
recommendations.rationale: No model clears the QS review evidence gates, so this API exposes the conservative demanding-analysis policy baseline, not an evidence-derived QS winner.

evidence.summary: Zero eligible operational runs; the sole fixture is excluded and every per-model quality line remains insufficientEvidence.

recommendations.label: HTML/UI implementation
recommendations.definition: Implementing a browser-rendered interface from content, interaction, responsive, accessibility, and visual requirements.
recommendations.outcomeMeasure: Rendered desktop/mobile defect checklist plus blinded jury-model quality score; critical accessibility or overflow defects fail the outcome.
recommendations.benchmarkStatus: Controlled two-scenario pilot complete; below the 20-attempt and five-scenario qualification gates.
downgradeWhen: The component is reversible and contained to one frontend subsystem.
Existing design tokens/components and a deterministic visual regression seam are supplied.
The concrete card score is at most 50 and no hard floor applies.
neverDowngradeWhen: A cross-application design-system contract or three runtime subsystems requires at least Sol/medium.
A jury score alone cannot waive a deterministic accessibility defect.
recommendations.rationale: Sol/medium passed both rendered scenarios with mean qualityScore 0.9175. Terra/medium also passed both but averaged 0.86125; Sol/xhigh passed one of two, averaged 0.82, and had one critical jury defect. The small, single-jury cohort makes this a pilot recommendation, not a validated universal winner.

costPerSuccessfulOutcome.note: Catalog list-price estimate for subject-model usage per passed rendered outcome. The fixed jury consumed 31,074 additional tokens across the two Sol/medium cases; component-level jury usage was not retained, so its dollar cost remains explicit unknown rather than an invented zero.

evidence.summary: Desktop/mobile rendering, deterministic checks, and fixed blinded jury; Sol/medium qualityScore 0.97.
Independent form genre; Sol/medium qualityScore 0.865 and no critical defect.
Versioned defect checklist, fixed jury route, blinding rules, pass threshold, gates, and limitations.

recommendations.label: Source-code review
recommendations.definition: Reviewing a bounded source change for correctness, reliability, security, and maintainability defects without implementing it.
recommendations.outcomeMeasure: Seeded-defect recall, severity-weighted recall, finding precision, and false positives against a hidden manifest.
recommendations.benchmarkStatus: Controlled two-scenario pilot complete; below the 20-attempt and five-scenario qualification gates.
neverDowngradeWhen: Ambiguous or unbounded authorizing evidence requires at least Sol/medium.
QS confirmation rate is not a substitute for seeded-defect recall.
recommendations.rationale: Terra/medium detected all 10 seeded defects, passed both scenarios, and cost about $0.030434 per passed outcome. Sol/xhigh also detected all 10 but cost about $0.164714 per passed outcome; Sol/medium detected 9 of 10 and passed one of two. This bounded pilot does not lower concrete-card security or ambiguity floors.

costPerSuccessfulOutcome.note: Catalog list-price estimate for Terra subject usage per passed outcome. Verification is deterministic local scoring and adds no model-token cost.

evidence.summary: Terra, Sol/medium, and Sol/xhigh each detected all five cache defects; Terra was cheapest.
Terra and Sol/xhigh detected all five transfer defects; Sol/medium missed one weighted defect.
Versioned hidden manifests, recall/precision scoring, gates, and limitations.
The per-model QS line has zero eligible operational runs and cannot contribute review recall.

recommendations.label: Security assessment
recommendations.definition: Assessing source, configuration, or architecture for exploitable weaknesses and security-boundary violations.
recommendations.outcomeMeasure: Seeded-vulnerability recall by severity, exploitability classification, false positives, and unsafe-remediation rate.
recommendations.benchmarkStatus: Planned slice; correctness hard floor is active.
neverDowngradeWhen: Security boundaries are a canonical Sol/xhigh hard floor.
Quota or cost cannot lower the hard floor.
recommendations.rationale: The canonical routing policy requires Sol/xhigh for security boundaries while controlled assessment evidence remains open.

evidence.summary: Security boundaries explicitly require Sol/xhigh; no cost or quota rule can cross that floor.

recommendations.label: Redundancy detection
recommendations.definition: Finding duplicated, overlapping, dead, or needlessly repeated logic while distinguishing intentional variants.
recommendations.outcomeMeasure: Seeded duplicate recall, precision, and semantic-equivalence classification.
recommendations.benchmarkStatus: Planned slice; canonical policy baseline is active.
downgradeWhen: The search corpus is one subsystem and duplicate candidates are mechanically enumerable.
The concrete card score is at most 50 and no hard floor applies.
neverDowngradeWhen: Cross-repository semantic equivalence or broad architecture context keeps the route at Sol/medium.
recommendations.rationale: Semantic redundancy detection is analysis with false-positive risk, so Sol/medium is the conservative baseline until the seeded suite establishes a cheaper winner.

evidence.summary: Broad-context analysis maps to Sol/medium; the class-specific controlled comparison remains a planned slice.

recommendations.label: Graphical-quality judgment
recommendations.definition: Judging visual hierarchy, polish, layout, and graphical defects in a bounded rendered artifact.
recommendations.outcomeMeasure: Agreement with a blinded multi-rater defect checklist and pairwise quality ranking.
recommendations.benchmarkStatus: Planned slice; bounded-decision policy baseline is active.
neverDowngradeWhen: Unbounded context or an ambiguous consequential decision raises the route to at least Sol/medium.
recommendations.rationale: A fixed screenshot, explicit checklist, and parseable verdict match the Mini/high bounded-decision role; the route is provisional until inter-rater study evidence exists.

evidence.summary: Mini/high is the bounded pipeline-decision exception over compact evidence with a deterministic output contract.

recommendations.label: Consistency checking
recommendations.definition: Checking repeated fields, behavior, terminology, or presentation for contradictions against explicit invariants.
recommendations.outcomeMeasure: Seeded inconsistency recall and precision against a hidden invariant manifest.
recommendations.benchmarkStatus: Planned slice; bounded-decision policy baseline is active.
neverDowngradeWhen: Unbounded context, derived requirements, or a consequential authorizing verdict raises the route to at least Sol/medium.
recommendations.rationale: A compact invariant set and parseable findings are a bounded Mini/high decision; open-ended consistency analysis must be rescored as research.

evidence.summary: Mini/high is permitted only for compact structured evidence and a deterministic output contract.
